public_sources.title: Time-sensitive anytime-valid testing
public_sources.authors: Eugenio Clerico; Tobias Wegel; Iskander Azangulov; Patrick Rebeschini
public_sources.used_scope: Hard-deadline anytime-valid testing is a sequential-control problem over time and evidence/wealth; asymptotic GRO can be strictly suboptimal when early rejection is the actual utility. The paper proves a Bellman reduction in its stated setting.

public_sources.title: Sequential testing of conditionally constrained hypotheses
public_sources.author: Eugenio Clerico
public_sources.used_scope: Predictable products of affine one-step e-variables form a complete class for the paper's finitely constrained conditional nulls, giving a lossless action parameterization for dynamic programming in that class.

public_sources.title: Safe testing
public_sources.authors: Peter Grunwald; Rianne de Heide; Wouter Koolen
public_sources.used_scope: A next e-variable may depend on information available before the next outcome, but validity requires the conditional e-variable property at that filtration; this pins down why outcome-derived side information is not free.

public_sources.title: Strong duality for the GROW criterion
public_sources.authors: Ashwin Ram; Martin Larsson; Johannes Ruf; Aaditya Ramdas
public_sources.used_scope: Worst-case log-growth over composite alternatives is a coherent robust criterion, but it optimizes a different objective from hard-deadline rejection.

post_outcome_sideinfo_counterexample.null: Let every fresh discordant sign X_t be +1 or -1 with probability 1/2 under the null.
post_outcome_sideinfo_counterexample.invalid_feature: Define a purported current-task covariate Z_t=1{X_t=+1}, which is only known after the fresh outcome, and set b_t=1 when Z_t=1 and b_t=0 otherwise.
post_outcome_sideinfo_counterexample.factor: The affine factor e_t=1+b_t X_t then equals 2 on candidate wins and 1 on incumbent wins, so E[e_t]=1.5>1. The process is not an e-process despite using an algebraically valid-looking affine form.
post_outcome_sideinfo_counterexample.measurement_rule: For every feature used to choose the fresh bet, record an availability timestamp/causal provenance and require it to be measurable before the paired outcome/judge label it will weight. 'Task metadata' is not sufficient if the metadata itself was produced after seeing the outcome.

rectangularization_penalty.structured_ambiguity: The three-map set from the previous checkpoint is {(q_low,q_high)=(.60,.80),(.70,.70),(.80,.60)}, which preserves the cross-stratum relation q_low+q_high=1.40.
rectangularization_penalty.rectangular_hull: Replacing that set by independent marginal intervals [0.60,0.80]^2 adds the unattested corner (.60,.60). Under worst-case log-growth the rectangular solution is simply q_bet_low=q_bet_high=.60, with expected growth about .008054 nats/task.
rectangularization_penalty.comparison: The structure-aware fixed-map minimax solution from the prior checkpoint achieved about .025236 nats/task worst-case, so rectangularization cut the guaranteed log-growth by about 68% in this stylized example.
rectangularization_penalty.scope_guard: Rectangular ambiguity is useful for dynamic consistency, but if the true uncertainty has cross-context structure, blindly rectangularizing it can erase precisely the side information one hoped to exploit.

hard_deadline_rectangular_bellman.setup: Use the stronger rectangular alternative q_t>=.60 on every discordant sign, average discordance rate .40, threshold 20 (alpha=.05), and horizon T=50. Optimize predictable affine bet b in [0,.999] by backward dynamic programming on a 600-point log-wealth grid with 161 candidate bet sizes. This is a numerical approximation, not a closed-form theorem.
hard_deadline_rectangular_bellman.policy_shape: At start wealth=1 with 50 tasks remaining, the approximate optimal b was .493 (q_bet about .747). At wealth=1 with 30 remaining b≈.642; with 20 remaining b≈.999. Near the deadline, states too poor to reach threshold under remaining bounded gains optimally stop risking wealth (b≈0), while reachable states use bold bets. This reproduces the time-sensitive shift away from stationary GRO/Kelly behavior.
hard_deadline_rectangular_bellman.robust_value: Under the design worst case q=.60,rho=.40, the Bellman value at wealth 1 was about .2015 reject-by-50. Direct simulation of the discretized policy gave about .1972 reject-by-50 versus about .0021 for stationary q_bet=.60 and about .113 for stationary q_bet=.75 in the same q=.60,rho=.40 setting.
hard_deadline_rectangular_bellman.null_sanity: 200,000 null trajectories with q=.50,rho=.40 gave crossing about .0459; with Markov-correlated task difficulty driving rho=.2/.6, crossing was about .0418. The conditional e-factor proof is the validity argument; these are implementation checks only.
hard_deadline_rectangular_bellman.structured_map_stress: Applied unchanged to the three structured maps at T=50, the approximate robust Bellman policy rejected about .689 correct, .510 flat, and .338 inverted. In the prior checkpoint, stationary fixed q=.75 gave .535/.356/.211, equal-weight map mixture .504/.285/.151, and structure-aware GROW minimax .193/.176/.161. Thus the finite-horizon robust policy dominated those tested stationary policies on reject-by-50 in every map despite being designed against the harsher rectangular q>=.60 alternative.
hard_deadline_rectangular_bellman.scope_guard: This comparison is against a small set of stationary/mixture baselines, not against the optimal finite-horizon policy for the nonrectangular fixed-map ambiguity set. Grid discretization and the assumed known discordance process can affect the numerical values.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Before a task-side feature can choose an e-bet, require machine-checkable evidence that the feature existed before the fresh paired outcome/judge label it will weight. Reject post-outcome or descendant features from the predictable betting filtration.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Direct fair-sign counterexample gives E[e]=1.5 when an outcome-derived feature controls the bet; Safe Testing supplies the conditional-e-variable requirement.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: A pre-outcome feature may still be unsafe if the conditional null fails after conditioning on it; timing provenance is necessary, not sufficient.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: For bounded paired-sign evidence with a short audit budget, optimize the predictable affine bet as a function of remaining horizon and current e-wealth under a prespecified conservative alternative/ambiguity set instead of using stationary GRO/Kelly bets.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Time-sensitive testing theory motivates the control objective; worker-local T=50 Bellman approximation raised worst-design q=.60 reject-by-horizon from ~.2% for stationary q=.60 and ~11.3% for stationary q=.75 to ~19.7%, while null crossing remained below .05 in simulation.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Numerical policy is specific to alpha=.05, T=50, rho=.40, q>=.60 and the chosen wealth/action discretization. It is not a universal bet schedule.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Represent transfer uncertainty with its cross-task-family constraints instead of automatically taking a rectangular product of marginal intervals; separately test whether dynamic-consistency convenience is worth the added unattested alternatives.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: In the stylized three-map set, rectangularization added (.60,.60) and reduced GROW worst-case log growth from ~.02524 to ~.00805 nats/task.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: A rectangular set may be appropriate when environment shifts can independently alter each stratum; preserving correlation without evidence can itself be overconfident.

rejected_or_narrowed_generalizations: Rejected: 'any feature that describes the current task is predictable side information.' An outcome-derived feature can make a nominal affine sign factor have expectation 1.5 under a fair null.
Rejected: 'worst-case GRO is enough for a short audit budget.' A hard-deadline Bellman policy was dramatically more powerful in the tested T=50 setting while retaining anytime-valid null control.

Narrowed: 'rectangular ambiguity is conservatively safe and therefore preferable.' It is conservative for the included alternatives but can impose a large power penalty by adding cross-context combinations that the structured uncertainty model ruled out.

Narrowed: 'a stationary q=.75 sign bet is already near-optimal for q≈.6.' It was much better than stationary q=.6 at T=50 but still far below the time/wealth-aware Bellman policy in the tested design.
Rejected: 'side-information value should be judged only by average power.' The filtration/provenance condition is a validity gate that must be checked before any power comparison.

frontier.action: Solve or approximate the finite-horizon policy for the original nonrectangular three-map ambiguity set, where nature chooses one fixed transfer map rather than a worst map independently each round. Compare least-favorable-prior/Bayes dual formulations, minimax regret, and rectangular Bellman policies under the same reject/harm/unresolved utility.

Generalize the filtration-provenance gate to real agent evaluation traces: enumerate which task metadata, judge features, retrieval traces, latency/tool outcomes and retry indicators are known before versus after the paired label. Construct a causal/temporal schema that can be validated from receipts.

Move reused-development candidate evaluation from fixed-horizon e-values to actual anytime PACE paths, charging stopping time/running supremum/returned metadata in the selectable transcript and keeping candidate-generation selection validity separate from within-candidate optional stopping.

Add repeated candidates sharing the same fresh tasks and quantify run-level multiplicity under cross-candidate dependence; compare e-closed testing, alpha spending and dependence-robust e-value multiple testing on top of candidate-valid factors.

Stress the time-sensitive policy under misspecified discordance rates, missing transfer maps, task-family Markov shifts and asymmetric harmful-commit cost; distinguish robustness of null validity from robustness of utility/power.

frontier.exact_next_action: Treat the structured transfer map as a fixed latent environment rather than rectangular per-step ambiguity, find a least-favorable prior or minimax-regret finite-horizon paired-sign policy, and compare it against the rectangular Bellman policy while preserving the newly explicit filtration-provenance gate.
